items.level_reason: Same shape as the official one-fact KNM questions on work: a body is named and the learner picks it from three institutions. The key is a well-known word.

evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid, 'Wat is een cao?' (opened 2026-11-22), section 'Wie sluit een cao af': 'Een cao wordt afgesloten door 1 of meer werkgevers, 1 of meer werkgeversorganisaties en 1 of meer werknemersorganisaties (meestal vakbonden).' Distractors: an ondernemingsraad exists inside one company and is not a cao party; the UWV pays benefits. Both false. Key (B) is neither the longest nor the only plural; the prompt says 'organisaties' and the card 'werknemersorganisaties', which both options do not echo.

meaning.situation_summary: Sanne stacks boxes in a warehouse and works under a cao; the question asks who concludes that cao for employees like her.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A working person learns that unions, not the works council or the UWV, agree the cao with employers.
meaning.contrivance_check: The picture is a warehouse and shows no organisation, so no option is revealed. Mentioning a cao in the prompt is a natural work fact; no off-page event is needed.

items.level_reason: Persona fact with one rule; slightly harder than the official 'who pays' items because three institutions are plausible, but each is clearly distinguishable.

evidence.quote: De regel is dat de werkgever de WW-premie betaalt aan de Belastingdienst
evidence.summary: Belastingdienst, 'Hoe betaalt u mee aan de premies werknemersverzekeringen?' (opened 2026-11-22): 'De regel is dat uw werkgever of uitkeringsinstantie de premies werknemersverzekeringen betaalt. Hierop is 1 uitzondering: ... Werkhervattingkas (Whk).' Same site, 'Werknemersverzekeringen' (opened 2026-11-22) lists the Werkloosheidswet (WW). The Whk premium is not the WW premium, so no distractor is true. Distractors: 'Mohammed zelf' is false; the UWV pays the WW benefit, not an employee's premium. Prompt no longer contains 'werkt', so 'werkgever' is not echoed.

meaning.situation_summary: Mohammed has a job at a building company and the question asks who pays the WW premium to the Belastingdienst for him.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A worker learns that his employer, not he himself, pays the WW premium.
meaning.contrivance_check: The prompt states the job in a plain clause and the picture shows a building site with a helmet, which does not show who pays. 'Volgens de regel' covers the one Whk exception on the page.

items.level_reason: One of two named bodies on the page is keyed; the other two options are agencies with obviously different jobs, so the item is comparable to the official 'where to get help' questions.

evidence.quote: bijvoorbeeld bij het Juridisch Loket of bij uw vakbond
evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid, 'Wat kan ik doen als ik ongelijk behandeld word bij een sollicitatie of op het werk?' (opened 2026-11-22): 'juridisch advies inwinnen, bijvoorbeeld bij het Juridisch Loket of bij uw vakbond'. The Juridisch Loket is not an option, so only one option is true. Belastingdienst (taxes) and Kamer van Koophandel (company register) give no advice on discrimination; both false.

meaning.situation_summary: Bilal sits at an office desk looking at papers because he thinks he is discriminated against at work; the question asks where he can get advice about his rights.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A person who feels discriminated against learns that a union can give advice.
meaning.contrivance_check: The question says only that he thinks he is discriminated against; the picture of papers shows no organisation. The key is a body that exists for employees, so no invented event is needed.

items.level_reason: The key 'Zij zelf' follows from the word zzp'er (self-employed), so it is easier than an official institution question; accepted as a fact item.

evidence.quote: Extra pensioen naast de AOW kan een zzp'er zelf regelen
evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid, 'Hoe regel ik mijn pensioen als zzp'er?' (opened 2026-11-22): 'Als zzp'er heeft u recht op AOW als u de AOW-leeftijd bereikt. U kunt daarnaast zelf uw oudedagsvoorziening aanvullen.' The page names a lijfrente at a bank, insurer or investment firm. Distractors: a client (klant) has no duty; the gemeente has no role. A few professions have a compulsory pension fund, but even then no client arranges it. CHECK YEARLY (mandatory AOV and Zelfstandigenwet in progress; not tested).

meaning.situation_summary: Iris works as a self-employed person at a laptop at home and asks who arranges her extra pension next to the AOW.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A self-employed person learns that she arranges extra pension herself, because no employer does it.
meaning.contrivance_check: The prompt names the status (zzp'er), the AOW is the stated baseline, and a home desk shows no pension provider, so the scene supports the fact without an off-page event.

items.level_reason: Closer to an A1/A2 common-knowledge fact than most KNM items; the bill going to the insurer is stated in the card and the distractors are clearly false, so easier than the official health questions.

evidence.quote: De huisarts stuurt de rekening direct naar uw zorgverzekeraar
evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid, 'Moet ik de huisartskosten zelf betalen?' (opened 2026-11-22): 'Uw zorgverzekeraar betaalt rechtstreeks de rekening van uw huisarts.' Second page 'Zorgnota controleren' (same day): 'Een zorgverlener stuurt een rekening meestal rechtstreeks naar uw zorgverzekeraar.' Distractors: a bill sent to Kofi at home and to the gemeente are both false for a huisarts visit. Not the eigen-risico fact of batch 006.

meaning.situation_summary: Kofi waits in a calm waiting room before a GP appointment; the question asks where the GP sends the bill for this visit.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A patient learns that the GP bills the health insurer and he gets no bill at home.
meaning.contrivance_check: A waiting room with a plant and a door shows no bill or insurer. Asking about the bill before a visit is natural for someone new to the system.

items.level_reason: The learner must tell a bill sent directly by the provider from a bill that stands online at the insurer; the insurer is a real confusion, so harder than a plain institution question.

evidence.quote: Stel uw vraag dan aan die zorgverlener
evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid, 'Hoe kan ik mijn zorgnota controleren?' (opened 2026-11-22): 'Heeft u een vraag over een rekening die u direct ontvangen heeft van de zorgverlener? Dan kunt u met uw vragen terecht bij de zorgverlener.' and, for a zorgnota in 'mijn omgeving' of the insurer, 'terecht bij uw zorgverzekeraar'. Distractors: the zorgverzekeraar is false because the prompt says the bill came directly from the provider; the huisarts did not send the bill. The key repeating 'fysiotherapeut' no longer stands alone because the insurer is a real alternative. Not a repeat of 006 zorgnota.

meaning.situation_summary: Mariam sits at a kitchen table with an opened envelope and does not understand an amount on a bill from her physiotherapist; the question asks to whom she puts her question.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A patient learns to ask the provider that sent the bill, and the insurer only when the bill is online there.
meaning.contrivance_check: The envelope and sheet in the picture show a bill but no sender. The prompt states the sender and the doubt, so no off-page event is needed.

items.level_reason: A single everyday fact with an obvious shop for the key; easier than the official medication questions, which tend to involve the apotheek and a recept.

evidence.quote: Deze zijn ook bij de drogist of andere winkels te koop
evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid, 'Waar kan ik medicijnen kopen?' (opened 2026-11-22): 'Receptmedicijnen kunt u alleen bij een apotheek kopen. Voor zelfzorgmedicijnen heeft u geen recept nodig. Deze zijn ook bij de drogist of andere winkels te koop.' The apotheek is not offered, so no option is also true. Some zelfzorgmedicijnen (UA) are only at the apotheek; the card says 'ook', so nothing conflicts. Distractors: the tandarts and the fysiotherapeut do not sell medicines; both false.

meaning.communicative_purpose: A person with a cold learns that no prescription is needed for self-care medicines and that a drogist sells them.
meaning.contrivance_check: The sofa scene shows illness but no shop, so the key is not pictured. Wanting a cold remedy without seeing a doctor is an ordinary reason to ask.

items.level_reason: A numeric advice item with three clearly different frequencies; comparable to the official 'how often' questions. The advice is stated as advice by the huisartsen, not as a rule.

evidence.quote: ga elk jaar 1 of 2 keer naar de tandarts voor controle
evidence.summary: Thuisarts (Nederlands Huisartsen Genootschap), 'Ik wil mijn tanden goed verzorgen' (opened 2026-11-22; revised 14 April 2026): 'Ga elk jaar 1 of 2 keer naar de tandarts voor controle.' Acceptable source: NHG is the professional body of the huisartsen and runs Thuisarts; the page is the standard public advice. No government page states the frequency (rijksoverheid.nl pages on tandartszorg returned 404). Distractors: every month and once in five years are not the advice. Key is not the longest option.

meaning.situation_summary: Kofi sits in a dentist's chair and wants to keep his teeth healthy; the question asks how often huisartsen advise a dental check.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A person learns the usual advice of one or two dental checks a year.
meaning.contrivance_check: The dentist chair does not show a number. The question names the advising body (huisartsen), so the card can say who gives the advice without an invented rule.

items.level_reason: Persona fact on referral, equal in demand to the official health-care institution questions; the term ggz is explained on the card.

evidence.quote: Dan kan de huisarts hem doorverwijzen naar de ggz
evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid, 'Psychische hulp: huisarts of ggz' (opened 2026-11-22): 'De huisarts is verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling van lichte psychische klachten. En kan mensen met matige tot zware psychische problemen doorverwijzen naar zorgaanbieders binnen de ggz.' Other professionals (bedrijfsarts, specialist) can refer too; neither is an option. Distractors: a werkgever and a zorgverzekeraar cannot refer; both false.

meaning.situation_summary: Esther sits calmly across a doctor at a desk and has heavy psychological complaints; the question asks who can refer her to the ggz.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A patient with serious problems learns that the huisarts is the door to specialised mental health care.
meaning.contrivance_check: Two people listening calmly shows a consultation with no distress and no answer. The prompt gives the complaint and the card the rule, so nothing off-page is needed.

items.level_reason: Matches the official emergency-care questions: the prompt sets up the condition (Saturday, no danger) and asks for the first contact.

evidence.quote: Neem dan altijd eerst contact op met de huisartsenpost
evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid, 'Huisartsenpost en spoedeisende hulp' (opened 2026-11-22): 'Neem altijd eerst contact op met uw huisartsenpost voordat u naar de spoedeisende hulppost gaat. Behalve bij een levensbedreigende situatie. Dan kunt u het beste direct 112 bellen.' The condition rule holds: the prompt states 'niet in gevaar'. Distractors: 112 is for danger to life; the spoedeisende hulp is not the first contact. The 1 January 2027 billing change is not used.

meaning.situation_summary: Thijs sits on the sofa on a Saturday with stomach pain, his life is not in danger and the practice is closed; the question asks whom he contacts first.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A person with an urgent but not life-threatening problem outside office hours learns to call the huisartsenpost first.
meaning.contrivance_check: Saturday explains why the practice is closed and the prompt excludes danger, which is the only exception on the page. The picture shows daylight and a phone but no clinic.

items.level_reason: One term to recognise (PGO); the card explains it and the term is built from plain parts (persoonlijk, gezondheid, omgeving), so the item is comparable to official term items though the term is new.

evidence.quote: Dat kan online in uw persoonlijke gezondheidsomgeving (PGO)
evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid, 'Mag ik mijn medisch dossier inzien?' (opened 2026-11-22): 'online in uw persoonlijke gezondheidsomgeving (PGO); bij uw arts of zorginstelling.' Distractors: the Belastingdienst and the gemeente hold no medical file, so their online portals are false. The key contains 'gezondheid', which makes the key guessable from the topic, but the PGO is the tested term and all three options are named places 'in de online omgeving'.

meaning.situation_summary: Sanne sits on the sofa with a tablet and wants to look at her medical file online; the question asks where that is possible.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A patient learns that she may see her own medical file in a personal health environment (PGO).
meaning.contrivance_check: A tablet on the sofa shows the wish to look online without revealing the PGO. Wanting to see one's own file is an everyday reason and the right is stated on the card.

items.level_reason: Institution item with plausible distractors (UWV, SVB are real benefit bodies); comparable to the official 'where to get help' questions. DigiD help is a current practical need.

evidence.quote: Dan kunt u terecht bij een toeslagenservicepunt
evidence.summary: Dienst Toeslagen (Belastingdienst), 'Hulp bij toeslagen zoeken' (opened 2026-11-22): 'U kunt ook bij de hulppunten terecht als u het bijvoorbeeld moeilijk vindt om uw toeslagen met DigiD te regelen.' and 'Al deze plekken kunnen u helpen met het aanvragen, wijzigen en terugbetalen van zorgtoeslag, huurtoeslag ...'. The term toeslagenservicepunt appears in the page link and URL; the card uses it as the name of these hulppunten. Distractors: UWV (uitkeringen) and SVB (AOW, kinderbijslag) do not help with toeslagen; both false.

meaning.situation_summary: Iris sits at a kitchen table with a phone and a puzzled look because DigiD makes her zorgtoeslag hard to arrange; the question asks where she can get help.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A person who struggles with the online allowance process learns that a service point helps in person.
meaning.contrivance_check: The puzzled face over a phone shows the difficulty, not the place. Naming zorgtoeslag and DigiD in the prompt matches the official page, so no off-page event is needed.

items.level_reason: The key 'de gemeente' is the commonest KNM key; the distractors (huisarts, woningcorporatie) are clearly unrelated, so easier than the official institution questions.

evidence.quote: Voor hulp bij uw schulden kunt u zich melden bij uw gemeente
evidence.summary: Rijksoverheid, 'Waar moet ik schuldhulpverlening aanvragen?' (opened 2026-11-22): 'Voor hulp bij uw schulden kunt u zich melden bij uw gemeente. U kunt daar terecht voor een advies of een aanvraag voor schuldbemiddeling of schuldsanering. De gemeente kijkt of ze u kan helpen bij uw schulden.' Distractors: a huisarts and a woningcorporatie do not offer debt help (a corporation may refer a tenant, but is not where one reports for debt help); both false.

meaning.situation_summary: Bilal sits at a kitchen table with a stack of envelopes and has many debts; the question asks with which organisation he can report for help.
meaning.communicative_purpose: A person in debt learns that he reports to the gemeente and is not left alone with the letters.
meaning.contrivance_check: The envelopes show the debts without any organisation. The tone stays calm: no distress is shown and the card states only where to go.
